subject: Commit modeling: Pegasus edgeburst SLA buffer proposal
messages:
From: Camilla Sørensen <camilla@pegasus.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: 2028-06-29T08:15:00Z
Subject: Unexpected edge bursts — need a commit buffer proposal

Hi Karthik / Neha,

Quick context: over the last 10 days we've seen multiple short-lived spikes from our edge agents — 30s bursts that are ~6x baseline token/sec for a tiny fraction of requests but are enough to push our hosted provider into throttles. We're evaluating a dedicated slab commitment with Redwood to guarantee latency and avoid timeouts.

Can you run a short modeling exercise that shows:
- tokens/sec baseline and burst assumptions mapped to required GPUs (NVIDIA A10-like baseline)
- p95/p99 latency fit for our 3 candidate model variants (pegasus-small, pegasus-medium, pegasus-large)
- recommended buffer (slab surge %) to keep p99 < 350ms during the short bursts

I've attached q2 traffic export (pegasus_q2_traffic.csv) with per-minute counts and a short narrative. Procurement is waiting for a buffer proposal before we lock down commit terms.

Thanks — Camilla
Camilla Sørensen
Head of Edge Ops, Pegasus Labs

Attachment: pegasus_q2_traffic.csv (CSV, 210KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Camilla Sørensen <camilla@pegasus.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-29T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected edge bursts — need a commit buffer proposal

Camilla — thanks for the export and the callout.

High level summary up front so procurement can move: with the traffic characteristics you sent, our simulation indicates that a dedicated slab sized for sustained baseline will see p99 spikes beyond 350ms when concurrent short bursts hit ~5–8x baseline token/sec if we provision no buffer. Recommending a 25% surge buffer (i.e., commit + 25% headroom) for peak safety with the following tradeoffs explained below.

What we ran (quick notes):
- Baseline qps/token mix pulled from pegasus_q2_traffic.csv; we modeled per-minute peaks and a burst-layer distribution (short bursts defined as events <60s)
- Serving assumptions: pegasus-small ~3k tokens/sec per A10-equivalent GPU, pegasus-medium ~7k t/s, pegasus-large ~14k t/s (these are conservative, network and kv-cache warm-up excluded)
- Latency model: we used Redwood's p95/p99 cost-latency curves for your typical generation length (avg 120 tokens) and included a small cold-KV penalty for burst start (adds ~35–60ms depending on model)

Preliminary recommendations:
- If you want to guarantee p99 < 350ms with <1% throttle risk, commit to capacity equal to baseline demand + 25% surge buffer using pegasus-medium as the default served model.
- If cost is more sensitive and occasional p99 breaches are tolerable, baseline-only commitment with an automatic burst fallback to a cheaper region/model is possible (we can draft the fallback policy).

Ben — looping you in for the detailed calc sheet and a sanity check on model tokens/sec assumptions; attaching a short calc workbook from our sim.

Next asks for you: could you share a 72-hour detailed sample (per-second if available) for one of the recent spike days? the per-minute file is helpful but per-second will tighten the headroom estimate. Also, are there constraints on model variant (can you use pegasus-medium for inference) or are you fixed to pegasus-large?

I'll attach our summary workbook in the next message.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: pegasus_edgeburst_calc_summary.xlsx (will follow)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Camilla Sørensen <camilla@pegasus.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-29T12:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected edge bursts — need a commit buffer proposal

Adding the calculation notes and the workbook. Quick technical highlights:

- Token/sec assumptions: validated on A10-profile: small=3k, medium=7k, large=14k (benchmarked with sequence lengths 80–160 tokens). These include 10% throughput delta for quantized kernels.
- Burst modeling: converted per-minute counts to a mix of 90% regular traffic / 10% short bursts. For the observed spikes we saw burst density ~0.7 events per hour on peak days.
- Buffer sensitivity: 15% buffer cuts throttle risk from ~12% -> ~5%; 25% cuts to ~1.2%; 40% is effectively insurance (0.1% throttle risk) but raises committed cost ~16% vs 25% buffer.
- Latency fit: with medium model and 25% buffer simulated p95=210ms, p99=320ms for typical spike pattern (KV warm-up included). Large model tightens p99 by ~40–60ms but doubles committed compute cost.

Recommendation for commercial review: peg a 12-month reserved slab sized to baseline+25% and allow a short 30-day canary after go-live where we monitor for real-world burst profile before finalizing commit ramp cadence.

Attaching: pegasus_edgeburst_calc_summary.xlsx (contains per-slab GPU counts, cost delta table, and Monte Carlo burst sim)

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pegasus_edgeburst_calc_summary.xlsx (Excel, 68KB)

From: Camilla Sørensen <camilla@pegasus.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: 2028-06-29T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected edge bursts — need a commit buffer proposal

Thanks Karthik / Ben — really helpful and clear. Procurement is comfortable with the 25% buffer recommendation for the initial commit window; they asked for 2 quick items before sign-off:

1) Please drop a short Mutual Action Plan (timeline + ramp + canary metrics) into the shared Drive link so procurement can attach it to the SOW.
2) Share a short summary (one paragraph) that the buffer is intended to reduce p99 throttle risk to ~1% during observed short bursts and that we will revisit after the 30-day canary.

We have an internal preference to run pegasus-medium in prod if the pricing delta vs large is >1.8x — otherwise, they may prefer the large model. I'll confirm by EOD tomorrow.

If you can add the MAP doc and the one-paragraph summary into the Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PegasusML-Shared/CommitModeling), procurement will start the SOW draft.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Camilla
Camilla Sørensen
Head of Edge Ops, Pegasus Labs
